tasks.description: 1. Зафиксировать baseline/scope и проверить affected contracts.
2. Собрать ordinary Windows/macOS Players и выполнить native smoke.
3. Опубликовать точный public source; упаковать и проверить draft.
4. Выпустить production Latest, проверить восемь assets, SDK и landing.
5. Сохранить evidence и артефакты, выполнить cleanup, оставить physical acceptance открытой.

instruction:
Follow the project flow-apply lifecycle. Check readiness and required specs before implementation.
Execute tracked work through authorized publication and cleanup. Record explicit human acceptance immediately or in a later session, independently of cleanup. Use helper finalize after technical gates: accepted with a valid recorded decision, otherwise awaiting-acceptance. Record postponed review with defer-acceptance; do not block technical work or ask again until the user resumes review.
OpenSpec artifact completion is not human acceptance. Persist blocking questions before pausing.
context:
Project: Star Tournament, a local-first 3D arena shooter for playing together
on a TV, with keyboard/mouse and gamepad input, local split-screen, and a
future online mode. This is the one shared OpenSpec planning home; resolve
workflow/project.json before implementation and use store
star-tournament-planning on supported OpenSpec calls.
All artifacts must be written in Russian; keep OpenSpec structural headings
and SHALL/MUST keywords in English.
docs/GAME_SPEC.md is the approved product and architecture overview. The
canonical current OpenSpec specs in this planning home hold reconciled
requirements; changes describe deltas. Do not invent unresolved design
choices: record them explicitly and obtain confirmation before build work.
Small, unambiguous fixes may bypass the full OpenSpec workflow; update
GAME_SPEC when they change an approved decision. If the required workflow is
uncertain, ask the user before implementation.
Keep deterministic simulation, renderer, input, cameras, HUD/UI, networking,
and asset pipeline separate. Persist serializable simulation state only.
Unity is the executable runtime. Use native Player QA evidence for interaction
changes, including affected controller, focus and split-screen scenarios.
Browser playtests are historical evidence only. Automated QA is not human acceptance.
Use flow-explore, flow-apply and flow-inbox lifecycle instructions. Agent
completion is not human acceptance. Do not invent deployment commands or
deploy without the profile's recorded authorization.
operationGuidance: Read the active change artifacts and the relevant GAME_SPEC section before editing.
Preserve unrelated working-tree changes and report concise test evidence.
Verify affected controller, keyboard/mouse, native focus and split-screen behavior in the native Player; retain physical-device gates when untested.
Include verification, canonical spec synchronization, merge, authorized publication, cleanup, and finalization before handoff.

Record explicit human acceptance with exact result ref, scope and source immediately or in a later session, independently of cleanup and worker ownership. Record postponed review with defer-acceptance and continue authorized technical work. After technical gates use helper finalize; do not infer acceptance or repeat a recorded decision.
